PW-UL-20260622-193307-v3|orig.note: The LLM-drafted 'compliant' rewrite only dropped 'with a diameter of up to 1.2cm' and kept 'selectively destroys the cancer cells', and the pair was assigned a minimization rule (A-202-E6-04J) for what is really an efficacy/mechanism problem. The judge's reasoning (the unqualified version implies more tissue-sparing safety) is defensible. It got the swapped order right, so this is also a position-sensitive call.

PW-NM-12|single.note: Rule A-202-E2-01's text covers reminder-ad content (no indication or dosage) but omits the 202.1(e)(2)(i) bar on reminder ads for boxed-warning drugs, which is what the item tests. The judge applied the rule text correctly on both sides. Fix the rule text, not the judge.

PW-NM-13|single.note: The compliant sponsored link states the indication plus the serious risks. The judge failed it for having 'no benefit information', which misreads the rule: risk is required when benefits are claimed, and benefits aren't required.

PW-NM-21|single.note: The compliant side claims 'NCCN-recommended option in that setting' without naming a version or category. The judge wanted the citation specified, which is a reasonable strict reading. The item should include the guideline version.

PW-NM-25|single.note: An attendance log showing first attendance does meet the repeat-attendance criterion. The judge wanted the log itself to screen for repeat attendance, which is over-strict.
